segments.he: אמר: הלא החנוני דרכו להקיף בהקפה, שיתנו לו לאחר זמן, ומדוע לא יאמר האדם איזה קפיטליך תהלים או ללמד או לעשות שאר מצוות, ויהיה מונח ומוכן אצלו לעת הצרך?! כי יהיה זמן שיצטרך לזה, שיגבה שכרו ופעולתו. לא יהא שנותן החנוני (נ"א ומדוע לא יהא כהחנוני שנותן סחורה בהקפה וכו' ?! ולא שמעתי שיחה זו בעצמי מפיו הקדוש רק מפי אחר. וכפי הנראה שהיה בזה שיחה נאה ולא זכיתי לשמעה):
segments.en: 272-4 Outpouring of the Soul 39. Designate a special private place to do hisbodidus It is very good for a person to have a room designated for him alone, to engage there in the service of Hashem, and particularly in hisbodidus and conversation between himself and his Creator. And he said, that even the sitting itself, that one sits in a room allocated for him alone, this also is very good. However, even someone who doesn't merit to have his own room, even still, he too can come up with many schemes to carry out this practice of hisbodidus and to speak between himself and his Creator. And he said, that under the tallis it is also like a private room, for when one lowers the tallis over his eyes, it is possible to speak between himself and his Creator whatever he desires. Also it is possible to express one's words before Him blessed He when he lies down in his bed and covers himself with a sheet, as pointed out above (article 23), that this was the practice King David r.i.p. chose for himself. It is also possible to sit with a book, and others will think that he is learning, and he can speak then between himself and his Creator. Additionally, many ruses can be found (by) he who truly desires to conduct himself in this practice of hisbodidus which is higher than everything, for it is an essential root of holiness and purity, as has been explained already many times. However, it is better for one to endeavor to have his own room, as mentioned above. (Words of Rabbi Nachman, article 272-4). He said:It is good for a person to accustom himself to be able to vitalize himself with some melody. For melody is something very, very great and exalted, and it possesses tremendous power to awaken and draw the heart of a person to God, may He be blessed. And even someone who cannot play music — even still, in his own home, and between himself and himself (-when alone in private), he can vitalize himself with some melody, according to his ability to sing it. For the greatness of melody is beyond measure. And it is already explained in the words of our Rebbe, of blessed memory, many exalted teachings regarding the subject of melody (see Tzaddik). And examine the end of the story of The Seven Beggars — there, some of the greatness of melody is alluded to. For it is explained there that the main healing of the king’s daughter who fell into a faint came through melody — that is, through the ten types of melody, as is explained there. Study it well and understand deeply how far these things reach. For the holy soul of every Jew is also called a “king’s daughter,” as is well known. And she is placed in the location within each and every individual, tired and weary and weakened by her sins — which are the ten types of arrows that the king who captured her shot and hurled at her, as is explained there. And it requires a tzaddik, a righteous person with great spiritual power, who is able to enter into all the places where she has fallen, and extract from her all ten types of arrows — and to know all ten types of knockings, in order to know how to bring about her healing. And to play all ten types of melody, because her essential healing comes through melody and joy. And study further there, drawing insight from insight.And the main thing is to derive from there good advice for returning to God in truth — for “It is not the learning that is essential, but the action.”(Pirkei Avot 1:17)
segments.he_nikud: אָמַר: הֲלֹא הַחֶנְוָנִי דַּרְכּוֹ לְהַקִּיף בְּהַקָּפָה, שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ לוֹ לְאַחַר זְמַן, וּמַדּוּעַ לֹא יֹאמַר הָאָדָם אֵיזֶה קַפִּיטְלִיךְ תְּהִלִּים אוֹ לִלְמֹד אוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת שְׁאָר מִצְווֹת, וְיִהְיֶה מֻנָּח וּמוּכָן אֶצְלוֹ לְעֵת הַצֹּרֶךְ?! כִּי יִהְיֶה זְמַן שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לָזֶה, שֶׁיִּגְבֶּה שְׂכָרוֹ וּפְעֻלָּתוֹ. לֹא יְהֵא שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הַחֶנְוָנִי (נ"א וּמַדּוּעַ לֹא יְהֵא כְּהַחֶנְוָנִי שֶׁנּוֹתֵן) סְחוֹרָה בְּהַקָּפָה וְכוּ'?! וְלֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי שִׂיחָה זוֹ בְּעַצְמִי מִפִּיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ רַק מִפִּי אַחֵר. וּכְפִי הַנִּרְאֶה שֶׁהָיָה בָּזֶה שִׂיחָה נָאָה וְלֹא זָכִיתִי לְשָׁמְעָהּ:
